payload.retro_drained: Killer met: the inbox went 29 -> 0 with a recorded disposition on every note - six resolved, two pulled into this line of work, six routed to i11, eight to i9, seven to durable homes (i6, the engine-determinizer note, the next full retro, the retro machine's guidance).
payload.goal: The close-and-merge split works: an iteration commits at its own milestones onto its own branch, and closing merges only live claims to trunk while the full record stays reachable by tag.
payload.pulled_in: (a) The split itself, from note-989ab09c39b0 and se-v2-design §4: milestone commits land on iter/<id>, the close produces a merge commit whose TREE carries only live claims, and the mandatory iter/<id> tag becomes the named handle on the events. (b) The pointer triple completed on grants and blessed nodes (design floor items 3 and 4), without which an evidence pointer dangles the moment evidence leaves trunk. (c) The empty-branch guard on shipMerge - it reported merged:true on a branch with zero commits, which is how i8c shipped without producing a commit. (d) The two provisioning gaps found by i8c and logged as RAID: a provisioned worktree carries no node_modules, so its verify cannot even typecheck, and it forks before uncommitted engine fixes, so it runs a stale engine.
payload.left_out: Backporting the existing iterations off disk, and teaching the board and projectState to resolve archived iterations from git with an immutable cache - both go to i5e, because this iteration changes how git is WRITTEN and that one changes how it is READ. The top-level machine rework (ad hoc / iteration planning / iterations, with a viewer-only archive) goes to i11, which the owner sequenced before i9. The board cleanup that the machine makes possible - dropping the now-duplicated iteration sidebar - goes to i9. Real parallel subagents wait until after i5e, per the owner's rule that the mechanics get fixed before anything is parallelized.
payload.rigor: Systematic with the design-input phase reduced, under se.decision-refine-mode: this iteration REALIZES an already-ruled design rather than deciding one. Struck with reasons: M1 vision drafting - se.vision is inherited by pointer, the delta is one line; M2 understand and M3 specify are compressed - the requirements are the design document's own bullets (tree = live claims only, tag mandatory, pointer triple, branch holds events); M4/M5 candidate generation and Pugh selection are struck outright, because se-v2-design §4 already names the architecture and there is no second candidate to score - re-deciding a ruled design would be decision theater. Kept at full strength, because DELIVERY never shrinks: M6 prove, since one mechanic is genuinely unproven - whether a merge commit can carry two parents while its tree omits the event paths, and whether those paths stay reachable afterwards; M7 build red-first; M8 validate; M9 ship. Any genuinely-new decision that surfaces still takes its own gate.
